transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-06
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Leo Martinez (Redwood SE), Evan Torres (CTO, PaperTrail), Maya Singh (Head of ML), Ben Park (DevOps), Ruchi Patel (Product PM)

Summary (auto): quick onramp, TTFT credits, and security gating items.

00:00:05 Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we scheduled 40 minutes, so we'll try and keep it tight. quick intro round?
00:00:14 Evan (CTO): yeah hi i'm evan torres, CTO at PaperTrail Labs. we do doc ingestion and compliance automation for finance.
00:00:20 Maya (Head of ML): maya here, leading the models side. we're evaluating ways to reduce latency for chat assistants and also keep data private.
00:00:27 Ben (DevOps): ben, infra, i'll handle networking and security questions.
00:00:31 Jordan: awesome quick agenda: 1) time-to-first-token, credits and quickstart 2) hosting options — hosted vs dedicated vs private 3) security checklist and next steps. Samira will chime in on benchmarks.

00:01:05 Samira (SE): hi! nice to meet you all. i'll show a short slide of TTFT expectations and then discuss bench approach.

00:02:12 Jordan: First, simple question — are you planning to start with a PLG/self serve trial or do you have procurement already lined up?
00:02:20 Evan: we're leaning PLG first. product team wants to prototype in 1-2 weeks, then we decide if we need reserved infra. so TTFT is critical.
00:02:31 Jordan: great. with Redwood's hosted API most customers get to first call within hours and to production prototype in a few days. we also give free credits for trial — usually enough for 10k tokens of testing and a small bench.
00:02:47 Ruchi (PM): when you say hours, what are the blocking items? keys? network?
00:02:52 Jordan: keys and onboarding. sign-up, create an API key, run a simple cURL or SDK call. Samira: latency expectations?
00:03:04 Samira: right — for typical chat models on hosted, p95 latencies vary by model, but for small prototypes you can expect ~200–400ms for lower-cost models and 100–300ms for optimized variants, depending on sequence length. caveat, these are approximate.
00:03:20 Maya: ok that's helpful. our use-case is multi-turn customer support with 512 token context frequently, so KV cache behavior and longer context performance matters.
00:03:31 Samira: yep, for 512 tokens we recommend trying an optimized model we host — we have RDW-optimized profiles, excuse me that is Redwood verified models, and we also do continuous batching to keep throughput low.
00:03:45 Ben: question — we have strict data residency policies, and we may need a VPC or private deployment. is that something we can move to after the PLG trial?
00:03:54 Jordan: absolutely. the usual flow is self-serve hosted for quick validation then Dedicated or Private for production. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and stronger isolation; Private is our VPC/on-prem option for regulated data.
00:04:10 Ben: is there a big lift to move from hosted to dedicated?
00:04:14 Samira: there's a migration path — same API surface, so code changes minimal. the ops work is provisioning and network setup for Dedicated or Private. we have a migration checklist we can share.

00:04:44 Jordan: about credits — we'll provision trial credits to your account, Jordan to confirm the amount, but we can get you enough to run a bench and a few prototype flows.
00:04:52 Evan: perfect. what do you need from us to spin that up?
00:04:56 Jordan: just sign-up link or email; we'll attach credits to the account. Samira will also send a bench script.

00:05:20 Samira: on benchmarks — we recommend a small harness: 1) sample payloads from your multi-turn tests 2) p95 latency and cost per token calculation 3) run against hosted optimized model and a quantized variant if you want lower cost. i'll attach the script and a Google Sheet template.

00:06:02 Maya: are quantized variants available on hosted or only on Dedicated/private?
00:06:07 Samira: we support quantized model variants on hosted for selected models; for the most aggressive quantizations, Dedicated and Private give more control. the Optimize toolkit will recommend a profile.

00:06:20 Ben: important: we require SAML SSO for all vendor consoles and KMS-backed encryption for keys. can you support that?
00:06:28 Jordan: yes — SSO/SAML for the Console is supported, and we integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated deployments; hosted can use Redwood-managed KMS but we can discuss BYOK for enterprise agreements.
00:06:40 Evan: SOC2?
00:06:42 Jordan: Redwood is SOC2 Type II — i'll attach the report. also we keep audit logs and per-route tracing in the Console.

00:07:05 Ruchi: what's the usual timeline for SOC2 review for a vendor?
00:07:08 Ben: from our side, it's usually a few days to a week to decide whether to proceed with pilot depending on legal team throughput.
00:07:15 Jordan: ok noted. i'll aim to get the SOC2 packet and a compliance FAQ by eod.

00:07:40 Samira: technical deep-dive note: if you do an initial hosted test and find latency spikes under load, two levers are typical: enable prefix/KV cache for multi-turn workloads and tune batching thresholds. both are config-level and don't require code changes.
00:07:58 Maya: prefix cache — can we persist KV cache across session restarts?
00:08:02 Samira: on Dedicated/Private there's more control; on hosted we do managed KV cache with some session affinity. we'll document specifics in the bench playbook.

00:08:25 Jordan: any blockers to getting the trial started right away?
00:08:29 Evan: internal procurement wants to understand cost delta if we scale past prototyping — i.e., hosted per-token vs Dedicated committed pricing.
00:08:38 Jordan: good question. pricing: hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is reserved capacity with lower unit cost at scale. i'll include a short comparative table in the doc.

00:09:05 Ben: what about privacy — is data used for model training on hosted?
00:09:10 Jordan: by default hosted API does not use customer data to train public models; we have options for data retention and strict logging controls. enterprise agreements can further lock that down.
00:09:22 Maya: do you have prebuilt SDKs for node/python?
00:09:25 Jordan: yes, SDKs in Node, Python, and Go. example code makes TTFT faster — sample app with an express route takes <10 minutes to wire.

00:09:55 Samira: quick demo note — if we run a 50-request bench with your 512-token flows, we can show cost per 1k tokens and p95 latency. would you prefer we run that or you run it?
00:10:07 Evan: we prefer Redwood runs the first bench so we can compare numbers quickly.
00:10:11 Samira: great, i'll need sample payloads and a test account.

00:10:25 Jordan: i'll provision credits now. do you have an email we should attach them to?
00:10:29 Evan: evan@papertrail.ai
00:10:31 Jordan: noted. i'll send the invite and credits.

00:10:44 Ben: network question: do you offer private endpoints for VPC peering for the hosted trial?
00:10:50 Samira: for short trials, usually not — hosted trial uses public endpoints with token-based auth. for VPC/private endpoints that's in Dedicated/Private flows and takes a bit of network setup. if you need to proof connectivity we can do a short-living Private demo environment, it's more of a sales-assisted flow.
00:11:09 Ben: ok good to know.

00:11:20 Ruchi: timeline wise, if we sign up to the credits now how soon can we have the bench results?
00:11:25 Samira: if we get sample payloads and credentials by Monday, i can run and share within 48 hours.
00:11:31 Jordan: action: Samira will run bench; Jordan will send credits.

00:12:05 — brief pause as Jordan shares a link in chat — "Quickstart guide / trial credits"

00:12:20 Maya: slight transcription weirdness — you said RDW-optimized earlier, did you mean "Redwood-verified"?
00:12:26 Samira: yeah my bad, Redwood-verified, sometimes the automated notes flip it.

00:12:45 Speaker 1 (Leo Martinez): small note on model variants — if you want to try the cheaper quantized variants we can switch the bench to a quantized profile and measure drop in latency and token cost. often cost drops 30–60% at a small quality delta, depending on prompts.

00:13:10 Maya: how do you help measure quality regression when swapping models/quantization?
00:13:14 Samira: we recommend evals and a small prompt set that you control. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions against a baseline prompt set and send alerts. we'll include that in the playbook.

00:13:40 Evan: on the legal side, if we go Dedicated later, do we still get the same API and console?
00:13:46 Jordan: yes same API surface; the Console has additional enterprise controls for RBAC and audit retention on Dedicated and Private.

00:14:05 Ben: uptime SLAs?
00:14:08 Jordan: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. hosted has a high-availability control plane but Dedicated is for guaranteed throughput. specific SLA numbers i'll attach.

00:14:30 Maya: curious about cost example — if we have 200k tokens/day at prototyping scale, what's rough hosted cost?
00:14:38 Jordan: depends on model; i'll add a table but ballpark: hosted for optimized open model might be X cents per 1k tokens — we'll put exact numbers in the deck.

00:15:05 Evan: ok this is good. two risk items from me: 1) procurement timeline 2) bench numbers that reflect our real load.
00:15:14 Jordan: understood; we can do a bench with realistic load and then discuss reserved committed sizing.

00:15:40 Ruchi: any compliance checklist we should expect?
00:15:43 Jordan: we'll share a compliance pack that includes SOC2, ISO if requested, data flow diagram, and security whitepaper.

00:16:12 Samira: one more technical note: for multi-turn chat with 512 tokens, enabling prefix cache reduces token compute and can cut cost by about 20–40% depending on repetition. it's in our Optimize suggestions.

00:16:40 Ben: any hard dependencies on their end to test? just sample payloads and access credentials?
00:16:46 Samira: yes sample payloads, a test API key, and ideally a small dataset for prompts. we don't need production data — synthetic data works fine.

00:17:05 Maya: we sometimes use chunks and embeddings pipeline upstream; will Redwood embeddings integrate with our vector DB?
00:17:11 Jordan: yes embeddings are standard; many customers push vectors to Pinecone, Milvus, or in-house DBs. we'll share SDK snippets.

00:17:40 Evan: can you summarize the steps we agreed to?
00:17:43 Jordan: sure — 1) Jordan: provision trial credits to evan@papertrail.ai 2) Samira: run bench with sample payloads and share sheet 3) Jordan: send SOC2 & security docs 4) Ben: confirm network constraints and whether they'll need VPC earlier 5) Customer: decide within two weeks whether to expand to Dedicated.

00:18:05 Ben: that matches our expectations.

00:18:25 Jordan: touching on a few edge cases — if you need private model hosting on-prem we can discuss an air-gapped package but that's a longer project. for now PLG hosted trial remains fastest.

00:18:50 Maya: one tiny practical question: does Redwood log prompt text in traces? we need to avoid PII leaks.

00:18:56 Jordan: by default prompt text is logged for debugging but you can disable or redact logs and set retention windows. enterprise agreements can set stricter defaults.

00:19:20 Ruchi: will you include an estimated runbook for moving from trial to pilot?
00:19:24 Jordan: yes a short runbook with steps, stakeholders and typical timelines.

00:19:50 Samira: okay i'll outline the bench: 1) run 3 ramps: light/medium/heavy 2) measure p50/p95/p99 3) compare two model variants 4) report token cost per 1k and per-session.

00:20:20 Evan: great. do we have any integrations for observability like Datadog?
00:20:25 Jordan: yes we have tracing hooks and can forward metrics to Datadog or Grafana via exporters.

00:20:44 Ben: firewall rules — what's the allowed IP ranges for hosted?
00:20:47 Samira: we'll send the IP ranges but it's easier to use token auth from your app; if you need IP allowlists we can provide the ranges.

00:21:10 — short silence as notes moved —

00:21:20 Jordan: any competitor concerns? Maya?
00:21:24 Maya: we looked at OpenAI and Bedrock; main reasons to consider Redwood are observability and smoother transition to Dedicated/Private. also cost control levers.
00:21:38 Jordan: good to hear. we'll provide a competitor comparison doc as part of the packet.

00:22:05 Samira: if it's helpful, for the bench we'll include a quantized-run and a baseline so you can see quality deltas.

00:22:30 Evan: ok let's talk timeline — we hope to decide on pilot within two weeks. is that feasible if we get bench numbers quickly?
00:22:38 Samira: yes if we get payloads by Monday, bench in 48 hours, decision within two weeks is realistic.

00:22:55 Jordan: final logistics: i'll send a calendar invite for a bench review the week after.

00:23:10 Ruchi: anything else on your side?
00:23:13 Ben: we'll check with security and give a go/no-go on the trial within 48 hours.
00:23:20 Evan: thanks, this was useful.
00:23:24 Jordan: thanks everyone. recap and next steps in chat.

— end of recorded portion —

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mislabels (RDW vs Redwood), filler words, and overlapping voices at 00:10–00:12. Shared artifacts: Quickstart guide (link posted in chat), Trial credits provisioning ticket, Benchmark template (Google Sheet link), SOC2 packet (PDF link noted).

Recap (auto-generated): PaperTrail will receive trial credits and a bench run by Redwood; bench results and security docs to be delivered within the agreed timeline. Decision on pilot expected within two weeks.
